A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BARK research. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures; relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression results, synthetic and applied Bayesian optimization experiments, posterior-sampling timings and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds toy regression experiments, continuous optimization benchmarks, GP-RBF regression comparisons and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed BARK procedure is unchanged: forest-agreement kernels, MCMC inference, marginalization over leaf values, domain-uniform splits, low-rank updates and integrated-UCB optimization remain. Added explanations and the revised GP-RBF baseline optimizer do not change BARK.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and tasks, adding smooth continuous optimization benchmarks, Hartmann (6D) and Styblinski-Tang (10D), and continuous, ordered-discrete and categorical toy regression examples. These extend the existing regression and optimization coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GP-RBF to the retained four-dataset regression comparison through Table 7 and compares alternating and enumerated GP-RBF variants together on XGBoostMNIST in Figure 6. The other main BO comparator families remain.

E3.justification: The reported GP-RBF optimization protocol changes substantially: v1 uses continuous relaxation with one-hot categorical encoding when enumeration is infeasible; v2 uses alternating continuous optimization and discrete local perturbations. This affects central benchmark comparisons. v2 also adds per-iteration fitting, acquisition-optimization and total-time measurements; the existing BO initialization and iteration budgets remain.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds diagnostic experiments examining nonstationary function modeling and predictions for unseen categories. Section 7.4 and Appendix F.2 substantially extend the earlier posterior-sampling timing comparison to BO fitting and optimization costs across methods and benchmarks. Existing depth-prior, sample-count and kernel-approximation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report BO medians and interquartile ranges across 20 runs, regression means and standard deviations, and the same sensitivity-study run counts. v2's expanded Figure 5 caption restates existing uncertainty reporting; added result rows do not introduce a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 5–6 replace GP-RBF results under the revised optimizer, putting it ahead of BARK on DiscreteAckley, DiscreteRosenbrock and CCOBench; these are not same-protocol gains. v2 adds continuous-benchmark, toy-regression and runtime results, plus GP-RBF regression scores—for example, Student Performance MSE 1.00 versus BARK's retained 0.73. Original Table 1 and posterior-sampling timing values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The kernel equations, computational derivations, posterior-sampling ratios, Laplace-limit proof, approximation-failure argument and optimization formulation are retained. v1 Appendices E–G correspond to v2 Appendices H–J; their relocation does not add theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: fully Bayesian tree-kernel inference, efficient sampling, explicit predictive uncertainty and competitive Bayesian optimization. The added introductory motivation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies wall-time as BARK's main limitation and recommends alternatives for cheap or fast evaluations, extending v1's narrower sampling-cost discussion. It replaces the explanation that GP-RBF performs worse under continuous relaxation with a more qualified competitiveness statement. New discussions explain nonstationarity, categorical correlations and settings favoring smooth GP kernels.

D1.justification: v2 names BoTorch's optimize_acqf_mixed_alternating routine and newly explains that the unchanged BART grid size was chosen to match BARK's optimization wall-time. Hardware, software versions, code access, sampling settings and solver parameters remain. The new parameter-summary table consolidates previously stated values.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wan et al. (2021) when discussing alternating optimization and Surjanovic and Bingham (2013) for the continuous benchmarks. New Table 2 systematically compares largely previously cited methods by surrogate, optimizer and domain support, refining rather than redefining BARK's research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are preserved. v2 adds introductory motivation, targeted experimental explanations, a wall-time subsection and an impact statement, while expanding and reorganizing appendix headings. This is a limited narrative revision rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial displays: toy-regression and continuous-BO figures, runtime panels, a related-work matrix, a parameter-summary table and a GP-RBF regression table. The XGBoostMNIST runtime panels appear in both the main text and appendix. Figure 1 is enlarged, Figures 5–6 receive layout and legend changes, and existing appendix figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the central empirical comparison with a more capable mixed-space GP-RBF optimizer, GP regression comparisons and smooth-function tests. New runtime evidence and explicit applicability limits make the performance claims more balanced and practically informative. These address important weaknesses in evaluating BARK's advantages and costs. Table 7's mistaken BART caption, despite clearly labeled BARK columns, is a limited clarity defect against these substantial gains.
